key_insight: SQGen is a full quantum image generator that uses a latent-modulated quantized tensor train to produce image-scale outputs directly on quantum hardware without a classical decoder.
engineering_relevance: The design targets NISQ constraints by improving trainability, keeping circuits shallow and gate-compatible, and preserving an end-to-end quantum inference path.
method: Promotes the QTT bond index into ancilla bond qubits so each circuit site acts locally on a bond register plus row/column physical qubits.
Adds latent modulation by factorizing each re-uploading rotation into a trainable main term plus an additive latent term.
Trains a differentiable classical model under gate-compatibility constraints, then maps operators one-to-one to native quantum gates for deployment.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports extensive experiments on image datasets and synthetic data showing stable training, end-to-end generation from shallow circuits, and promising feasibility on real quantum hardware.
watch_item: The approach still depends on careful gate-compatibility and hardware noise tolerance, so performance may degrade as circuit depth or device imperfections increase.
paper_title: SQGen: Structured Quantum Image Generation with Latent-Modulated Quantized Tensor Trains
